citation: Slaby, Jan. "The Other Side of Existence: Heidegger on Boredom." 2010, pp. 101–121. ****** UNVERIFIED: publication venue not present in the pdftotext extraction (running heads give only page number + "Jan Slaby"/title; no journal/volume metadata). Provisionally identifiable as a chapter in Flach & Söffner (eds.), Habitus in Habitat I: Emotion and Motion (Peter Lang, 2010) — verify against the source PDF's title page before final citation.
thesis: Heidegger's FCM lecture course offers a remarkable existential interpretation of three varieties of boredom that reveals an inextricable bond between the temporality of Dasein and existential significance, such that the draining of meaning in boredom just is the slowing/halting of time; reconstructing this analysis as a paradigm case of 'affective intentionality' illuminates human affectivity generally, though Heidegger's final, activist-existential payoff (a demand to answer profound boredom's 'message' with resolute action) is judged an unargued imposition, contestable via a Pessoa-derived counter-stance of affirmed depersonalized detachment.

sections.title: Unheaded introduction
sections.summary: States the 'other side of cognition' thesis for moods/emotions; previews Heidegger's tripartite boredom analysis and its temporality/significance payoff; introduces 'affective intentionality' (self-citing Slaby 2008; Slaby & Stephan 2008) as the chapter's theoretical lens.

sections.title: From states of consciousness to existential orientations
sections.summary: Develops 'existential orientation' (after Ratcliffe's 'feelings of being') as background structures distinct from character traits and foreground intentional states; glosses Heidegger's Befindlichkeit as this same structure, joined to Verstehen; introduces the hexis/Haltung analogy.

sections.title: Heidegger on Boredom — 3.1 Becoming bored by something
sections.summary: First form: railway-station and boring-book examples; held in limbo and left empty by a determinate external item withholding an expected fulfilment.

sections.title: Heidegger on Boredom — 3.2 Being bored with something
sections.summary: Second form: evening-invitation example; self-forming emptiness of a freely chosen but existentially irrelevant engagement; the 'standing Now' (stehendes Jetzt) and collapse of past/future into an isolated present.

sections.title: Heidegger on Boredom — 3.3 Profound Boredom
sections.summary: Third form: the 'undifferentiated no one'; total, situation-independent meaninglessness of world and self; 'telling refusal' (Versagen) as itself a 'telling' (Sagen) announcing Dasein's withheld possibilities; entrancement by the fused threefold temporal horizon; the call to resolute self-disclosure in the moment of vision (Augenblick) and to freedom.

sections.title: Concluding remarks
sections.summary: Recaps escalating depth across the three forms; contests Heidegger's demand that profound boredom's message be answered with resolute action as an unargued activist imposition; deploys Pessoa's Book of Disquiet as a counter-exemplar of affirmed dwelling in depersonalized detachment.

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: culminating construct; undifferentiated no one, total meaninglessness of world, mode of unrelatedness

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: full reconstruction via railway-station/boring-book examples; held-in-limbo + left-empty by a determinate item

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: full reconstruction via evening-invitation example; self-formed ('own-making') emptiness; standing Now

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: analogical only — existential orientation as middle ground between dispositional trait and foreground intentional state; not a 1:1 mapping onto the psychological binary

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: Dasein's default mode is 'being-away' (Weg-sein), non-attentive absorption; boredom intensifies flight into distraction

constructs.treatment: attenuated proto-signal reading via 'telling refusal is itself a telling'; reconstructed faithfully then judged over-extended by Slaby's own critique

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: draining of world/self significance, escalating across the three forms from local item to whole world

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: connective construct; dragging time (1st) / standing Now (2nd) / fused threefold horizon (3rd)

readings.claim: Boredom is an 'existential orientation' — a background structure of experience/thought/action — rather than a subjective feeling-state; distinct from both character traits and foreground intentional states.

Heidegger's Befindlichkeit (attunement) names this existential-orientation structure precisely, inseparable from understanding (Verstehen): each attunement is understanding and each understanding has its attunement.

The three forms differ in situation-relatedness and temporal structure: first bound to a determinate item and dragging clock-time; second self-formed via free engagement and a standing Now; third total, impersonal, decoupled from situation, entrancing the whole threefold horizon.
Beings' 'telling refusal' in profound boredom is itself 'a telling, i.e. a making manifest' — it announces the very possibilities it withholds, and ultimately the freedom of Dasein as such.
This disclosure culminates in a call to resolute self-disclosure in the moment of vision (Augenblick), through which Dasein is the free, responsible creator of whatever meaning its life has.

Heidegger's final move too aggressively forces a specific, activist understanding of existence onto profound boredom, implicitly construing non-resolute lingering as inauthentic without adequate argument.
Pessoa's Book of Disquiet supplies a counter-exemplar: an affirmed, undemanding dwelling within depersonalized, meaningless detachment that answers no call back to resolute action.

tensions.axis: restatement/exegesis of FCM (§3.1-3.3) vs. explicit contestation (§4)
tensions.note: Slaby's own chapter shifts register partway through: high-fidelity reconstruction of all three forms gives way to an explicit, source-authored critique of Heidegger's final activist move.

tensions.axis: boredom's disclosure as demanding resolute action vs. boredom's disclosure as permitting affirmed detachment
tensions.note: Heidegger's own reading vs. Slaby's Pessoa-derived counter-reading; unresolved by Slaby, offered as an open possibility.

tensions.axis: boredom-as-message/telling (proto-functional) vs. boredom-as-deficit (P/anticipatory-application: resonance with the cluster's later Elpidorou functional-vs-deficit debate axis, not cited by Slaby)
tensions.note: Slaby reconstructs Heidegger's 'telling refusal is a telling' faithfully but judges its activist payoff over-extended — a philosophically independent version of the caution Elpidorou's regulatory account will supply from cognitive science.
